events.text: Little New Year: the Kitchen God goes to heaven to report on your household. People smear honey on his lips so he says only sweet things.

effects.log: He will say lovely things. Probably.
He hears everything anyway.

events.text: A kitchen fire breaks out while a family is burning the Kitchen God's picture.

ok.log: Smoke, soot, and a saved house.

fail.log: You put it out, and singe your eyebrows.

effects.log: The house burns a little. The family is safe.

variants: A family burning the Kitchen God's picture sets the kitchen itself alight.

events.text: Stalls sell sticky malt candy for the Kitchen God, so his mouth is too sticky to say anything bad.

effects.log: It glues your teeth together for an hour.
A street of sticky, happy children.

events.text: A cook at the temple kitchen tells you what the monks really eat when nobody is looking.

effects.log: The cook slips you the best dumplings for a month.
It becomes a local legend.

events.text: Two master chefs challenge each other before the new year.

effects.log: Both dishes are perfect. You declare a draw and gain two friends.
He wins by one vote.

events.text: An old woman's stove is broken, and she cannot cook for the festival.

effects.log: Clay and patience. It works.

choices.text: Invite her to eat with you

effects.log: She tells stories all night.

events.text: A child asks what the Kitchen God will say about you to heaven.

effects.log: The child nods seriously.

choices.text: Say he will complain about your cooking

effects.log: The child laughs until they cry.

events.text: A new Kitchen God picture must be pasted up for the new year.

effects.log: A respectable Kitchen God.
He looks a little amused all year.

events.text: You are told to be very good because the Kitchen God is watching.

effects.log: For almost a whole day.

choices.text: Ask if he is watching right now

effects.log: Yes. You stop stealing candy.

events.text: A roadside shrine to the Kitchen God, covered in honey and ants.

effects.log: The ants are displeased. The god is not.
More ants. Also more luck.

events.text: The custom is to sweep away all the dust of the old year before the Kitchen God returns.

effects.log: Clean floors, clean luck.
A day of meditation. Everything is clearer.

events.text: You dream that you are in heaven, hearing the Kitchen God's report on you.

effects.log: Mostly good. A few notes about your temper.
He accepts. Heaven is very sticky.
